initiative.title: One diagram of a project's tables, links, calculations, and views
initiative.summary: An ER-style diagram that doubles as the model editor, in a very wide drawer like Rows, for projects and single tables: tables, fields, relationships, calculations, and views, with lineage both ways, in-place editing through the existing editors, and an Add source path.
initiative.next_action: Implement milestones 1–7 as stacked PRs, each with verification screenshots.

claims.text: One surface shows the whole project's backing definitions.
Node + edge + field-list presentation, ER-diagram style.
Shows tables, fields, relationships, and calculations.
Shows downstream usage of fields by view.
Single-table workspaces render as one table showing its fields.
A user can add a new data source from the diagram.
The diagram uses a very wide surface like the Rows viewer.
The diagram must look and feel right early; visuals lead the sequence.
The schema viewer doubles as an editor: whatever is editable can be edited from it.
Query steps are shown and edited in the diagram; it is the all-in-one model surface.
The layout fills the viewport's shape so the diagram reads without zooming or panning, while flowing left to right and top to bottom.

claims: earlier shape boundary: read-only, relationship editing below cut line
conflicts.resolution: Superseded by c10 on 2026-10-10; editing is in scope and reuses existing editors.

shape.appetite: Large: the diagram, an editor layer built on the existing editors, lineage, and one table-to-project promotion path. No new runtime dependency.
shape.problem: Project definitions, calculations, and view usage are spread across the Schema panel, Query panel, and view settings; nothing answers what uses a field.
shape.recommended_shape: Pure buildSchemaGraph model feeding a fixed-column SVG diagram in a wide drawer shared with Rows, for projects and single tables. Selection opens an anchored nonmodal inspector that edits fields, keys, relationships, and calculations through existing write paths; lineage focus and uses list; host-backed Add source with single-table promotion.
shape.counterproposal: Extend the existing Schema panel card list with per-field 'used by' lists and no diagram. Cheaper, but fails the explicit ER-diagram and crisp-2D intent; its usage model is the same, so the graph model is built first either way.
success_moves: Lead with a polished visual slice (tables, fields, relationships) drawn from data the project states directly, reviewed in screenshots at three widths and two themes with an impeccable pass.
Prove the editor model (selection, anchored inspector, one undo step per edit, read-only) on tables and relationships before lineage adds columns.

Reuse, never fork, editing: move relationship proposal and match counts out of ProjectSchemaPanel and step building out of QueryRelationshipBuilder into shared logic; open the existing calculation editor; use updateFieldSettings; route project edits through onProjectChange.
Keep buildSchemaGraph pure and tested, reuse incompatibleSettingsFields' walk as settingsFieldUsage, and draw unresolved references as stubs.
Use a hand-rolled, viewport-aware layout instead of a layout library: layered columns when they fit, else the same reading order wrapped to the viewport's shape.
Keep schema.onProjectChange, views, and onAddSource optional; promotion, the biggest saved-state change, comes last with a round-trip test.

first_proof.question: Does a hand-rolled diagram of tables, fields, and relationships in the wide drawer look and feel like explorEDA on real demo data?
first_proof.artifact: Schema drawer on the shop, World Bank, flights, and a CSV import; screenshots at 1280, 783, and 390 px in light and dark; impeccable critique.
first_proof.decision_rule: If cards read at a glance and lines land on the right rows, add selection and editing on this drawing next; otherwise iterate on visual language and ordering first.

rabbit_holes: General graph layout and edge routing
Forking editor logic between the Schema panel and the diagram
Query structure editing in the diagram
Per-keystroke undo steps from inline inputs
Parameterized queries with missing bindings hiding fields
Positional row keys through single-table promotion

decision_log.decision: Include single-table workspaces as one table node.
Use a very wide drawer shared with Rows instead of the wide side panel.
Add source from the diagram, host-owned file picking, single-table promotion keeps charts.
Visuals lead: milestone 1 is a polished drawing of tables and relationships; lineage model grows behind the drawing in milestone 2.
The diagram doubles as an editor; relationship editing moves from below the cut line into milestone 2; calculation editing in milestone 3.
Query steps are added, edited, and removed in the diagram (milestone 4).
Promotion starts a new project session; the single-table session stays restorable.
Layout is viewport-aware: layered columns when they fit, otherwise the same order wrapped into columns sized to the viewport's aspect ratio; lines that skip a column route around cards.

milestones.title: A polished diagram of tables and relationships
milestones.outcome: Schema toolbar button opens a finished-looking diagram of tables, fields, and relationships in a drawer shared with Rows, for projects and single tables. Cards and field rows carry stable IDs for selection.
milestones.proof: Layout unit tests; Rows unchanged; screenshots of shop, World Bank, flights, and a CSV import at three widths and two themes, with impeccable critique fixes applied.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Useful ER overview for both workspace kinds; no lineage yet.
milestones.rollback: Remove the toolbar entry; Rows keeps the shared drawer with no visible change.
evidence: Vitest: src/test/lib/schema/schemaGraph.test.ts (10 tests), WorkspaceToolbar schema test, ProjectSchemaPanel Open diagram test
Playwright screenshots of shop, flights, World Bank, and a single table at 1280, 783, and 390 px, light and dark
Real-input checks: Open diagram from the Schema panel, drag pan, zoom, fit, close by chart-strip click

milestones.title: Select and edit fields, keys, and relationships in place
milestones.outcome: Selection with an anchored inspector; field names, labels, units, types, entity keys, and relationships (drag or menu, with match counts) edited from the diagram through existing write paths.
milestones.proof: Shared relationship logic unit tests; ProjectSchemaPanel tests unchanged; one onProjectChange per confirmed edit; read-only hides controls; browser checks at three widths.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Diagram is a working editor for tables and relationships.
milestones.rollback: Pass readOnly or hide inspector edit controls; Schema panel list still edits relationships.
evidence: Vitest: relationshipEditing.test.ts, schema/__tests__/SchemaDiagram.test.tsx (rename is one change on Enter, remove names following queries, Escape clears without closing, read-only has no controls); ProjectSchemaPanel tests unchanged
Playwright real input at 1280 and 390 px: select field and line, remove and re-create a relationship by dragging field to field (8 matched), rename a field, Escape ladder
Single-table label and unit edits each one demo undo step

milestones.title: Queries, calculations, and views drawn and editable
milestones.outcome: Query and view columns with lineage, calculation, and usage edges from tested buildSchemaGraph; workspace and query calculations created and edited from the diagram.
milestones.proof: Model tests on the shop fixture; incompatibleSettingsFields tests unchanged; calculation edits validated with breakage warnings; screenshot review on World Bank and flights.
milestones.rollback: Hide the query and view columns; table diagram remains.
milestones.spike_result: evaluateAnalysisQuery with no tables throws on lookups (a missing source gives no fields), but with defined empty tables it returns the same fields and origins as a real evaluation for every shop query and runs on World Bank, flights, and Beijing. The static-walk fallback was not needed.
evidence: Vitest: schemaLineage.test.ts (usage roles, lookup traced to Customers.name, step lineage, calculated step inputs, broken calculation has no guessed inputs, missing view field stub, single-table usage card); SchemaDiagram query-calculation check; project and provider tests unchanged (95)

Playwright: field selection lights its view uses; view selection lights all uses; flights query calculation edits in place; Add calculation opens the calculation editor and Escape returns to the diagram
milestones.notes: Usage lines show only for the selection so the default view stays readable; flow wrapping keeps tables, queries, and views in their own columns.

milestones.title: Edit query steps in the diagram
milestones.outcome: Add, edit, and remove lookup, expand, summarize, filter, and calculate steps, and start new queries, from query cards; dependency warnings on removal.
milestones.proof: Builder and dependency unit tests; QueryRelationshipBuilder tests unchanged; shop demo browser flow adding a lookup, filter, and summary; Query panel shows the same steps.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Diagram is the all-in-one model editor.
milestones.rollback: Hide step edit controls; the Query panel still edits steps.
evidence: Vitest: stepEditing.test.ts (lookup appends and becomes output, expand opens a new view, unique calculation field and input check, typed filter values, removal names lost fields and broken views, the reading step stays); QueryRelationshipBuilder and Query panel tests unchanged

Playwright at 1280 and 390 px: add a lookup, a calculation (bad expression refused), and a filter on a query card; remove a lookup with the lost fields named; removal on the current view's query names that view; a diagram-added step shows in the Query panel
milestones.notes: Shipped through menus in the details panel. Not built: dragging a relationship line onto a query card (the menu path covers it), and editing query parameters, which stay in the Query panel; filters on an input say so.

milestones.title: Field focus traces lineage both ways
milestones.outcome: Selecting a field lights its lineage; inspector lists uses and jumps to charts and views.
milestones.proof: traceField unit tests; real mouse and keyboard checks in the browser.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Diagram with focus over the current view's usage.
evidence: Vitest: schemaTrace.test.ts (table field to view and view calculation, view calculation back to table, summary back through its input, relationships shown but not walked); SchemaDiagram uses list and Show chart, unused field message
Playwright: flights Departure delay lights its calculation and seven view rows, dims three cards, and Show focuses the Mean departure delay chart; shop Joined says Not used by any view

milestones.title: Usage across every view in the host
milestones.outcome: Optional views prop; demo passes its tabs; uses span all saved views.
milestones.proof: Field used only by a second tab lists that tab; relationship removal warns about it; omitting views still works.

milestones.title: Add a source from the diagram
milestones.outcome: Add source appends a table to a project, or promotes a single-table workspace to a project keeping its charts and layout.
milestones.proof: Promotion round-trip test; demo CSV workspace adds a second CSV and keeps its charts; hosts without onAddSource show no action; pnpm check.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Feature complete for both workspace kinds.
